elements.text: Read with care: the model already knows many MultiHop-RAG answers
elements.originalText: Read with care: the model already knows many MultiHop-RAG answers

elements.text:
With no retrieval at all (closed-book), the answer model gets more MultiHop-RAG comparison questions right than any method, and about
as many temporal questions as Agentic GraphRAG. So on MultiHop-RAG, Answered right mostly measures what the model already knows. The
gold-facts measures are the fair test of retrieval there, and Agentic GraphRAG leads on them. On HotpotQA bridge questions, retrieval
clearly helps. Closed-book results are on the results slides.
elements.originalText:

gold-facts measures are the fair test of retrieval there, and Agentic GraphRAG leads on them. On HotpotQA bridge questions, retrieval
clearly helps. Closed-book results are on the results slides.

elements.text:
Agentic GraphRAG finds the evidence best when a question links several documents by comparison or by time. For the other question
types, Normal RAG does as well and is simpler to run.

elements.text: Safe skill learning for network and IT operations agents.
elements.originalText: Safe skill learning for network and IT operations agents.

elements.text:
An agent that fixes network incidents can save what worked as a reusable skill, so it gets better over time.
Two things go wrong. It learns to blame a fault even when the network is healthy, because every real fault
rewards a confident diagnosis. And a poisoned ticket or log can teach it a bad skill, which it then runs with
full permissions.
elements.originalText:
An agent that fixes network incidents can save what worked as a reusable skill, so it gets better over time.
Two things go wrong. It learns to blame a fault even when the network is healthy, because every real fault
rewards a confident diagnosis. And a poisoned ticket or log can teach it a bad skill, which it then runs with
full permissions.

elements.text:
Grow a skill library on a network-incident test set. Every new skill starts as advice only. Permission to act
is a separate grant, earned by checks: where the skill came from, a replay in a sandbox, and no rise in false
alarms on healthy networks. Compare against no checks and against accuracy-only checks.
elements.originalText:
Grow a skill library on a network-incident test set. Every new skill starts as advice only. Permission to act
is a separate grant, earned by checks: where the skill came from, a replay in a sandbox, and no rise in false
alarms on healthy networks. Compare against no checks and against accuracy-only checks.

elements.text:
NIKA, a network troubleshooting benchmark with 54 issue types. FaulT-Bench, which sends tickets that claim
faults on healthy networks. Poisoned skills built from published attack patterns.
elements.originalText:

elements.text:
Same or better fault finding, no rise in false alarms, 5% or fewer poisoned skills reaching action while 85%
or more of good skills are kept. The test setup is released for others.

elements.text:
Networking (Juniper, Mist, Marvis). HPE's pitch for agents is that they act under governance. In one sentence:
the agent gets better without getting more permission.
elements.originalText:
Networking (Juniper, Mist, Marvis). HPE's pitch for agents is that they act under governance. In one sentence:
the agent gets better without getting more permission.

elements.text:
FaulT-Bench found the false-alarm problem but did not study learning agents. EvoMal and SkillJack show skill
poisoning, but their defences screen content or assume a human reviews every skill. We found no study of
learning agents on NIKA or FaulT-Bench.

Agent security. Prompt-injection defences for agents
that change infrastructure.

elements.text:
A boundary that stops injected actions (a command
hidden in a syslog line or a Wi-Fi client name) also
blocks legitimate changes. NetInjectBench: undefended
agents took unsafe actions in 82.5% of attacks; a
static allowlist cut that to 5% but blocked every
approved change. No one has measured this trade
against an attacker who adapts.

to run and wasted long search loops. Self-evolution
papers report average accuracy, not whether the same
question gets the same answer.
